reuse.why: It reuses getWorstCaseAmount and getApproxNumberThreshold, but adds a new getExpectedAmount instead of extending the existing getScheduledAmount, which already performs the missing/number/range dispatch for the API and the desktop client.

duplication.why: getExpectedAmount re-creates getScheduledAmount's null/number/range dispatch alongside it. The inline ternaries it replaces are removed, but the tree now has two competing 'expected amount' functions.

placement.why: The new rule sits in shared/schedules.ts next to the existing amount helpers, the right module.

scope.why: Focused on the amount sites, plus an _amountOp field on RawScheduleData. The forecast call adds a fallback (`schedule._amountOp ?? conditions.amount?.op`) that is slightly defensive.

maintainability.why: There are now two near-identical exported helpers with different rules. Callers of getScheduledAmount (api-models expectedAmount, Balance, the schedule tables) silently keep the old rule, so the next change has to touch both.

bypasses_abstraction.where: shared/schedules.ts getExpectedAmount sits beside getScheduledAmount instead of extending it, and api-models.ts and the desktop-client callers stay on the old helper.

disguised_duplication.where: getExpectedAmount restates getScheduledAmount's missing/number/range dispatch under a new name, with the approximate case added.

one_place.where: The approximate rule lives only in getExpectedAmount (used by preview, posting, action sync, forecast and template). getScheduledAmount, used by api-models expectedAmount and the desktop-client Balance, still applies the old rule.
